newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul Exchange to introduce new indices.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul Exchange to introduce new indices.

text.p: Istanbul Stock Exchange decided to introduce new types of indices due to the rise in the number of listed firms and the need to cover existing markets and sectors and a planned futures market, the Exchange said in statement on Thursday.
Beginning from January 2, 1997, the Exchange will create sectoral and market indices besides IMKB National-All, IMKB National-100 and IMKB National-30.
IMKB National-All will include national market shares except investment trusts.
IMKB National-100, which will replace the current composite index (IMKB-100), will be used as the main index for the national market.

IMKB National-30, to be used in the planned futures market, will consist of 30 shares chosen from among 230 national market firms having high market capitalisation and liquidity and the ability to represent their sectors. It will exclude investment trusts.
The contents of IMKB National-30 will be modified twice a year and IMKB National-100 four times.
Sectoral and sub-sectoral indices will also be developed.

IMKB National-Industrial index will comprise food and beverages, textile, leather, forestry, paper and publishing, chemicals, petroleum and plastic, soil-based, metal, metalware and machinery industries which will have separate indices.
Electricity, transportation, tourism and trade sectors and their indices will be covered under IMKB National-Services index.
Banking, insurance, leasing, factoring, holding and investment indices will be calculated as sub-sector indices under IMKB National-Financial.
Shares of 14 investment trusts listed on the Exchange will only be covered by the IMKB-investment trusts index.

Of the above, IMKB National-100, IMKB National-Industrial, IMKB National-Services and IMKB National-Financial will be broadcast during trade hours while the other indices will be disclosed at the end of the sessions.
The Exchange will also introduce indices for its regional and new company markets.
The calculation of indices according to weighted average prices will cease at the beginning of 1997.
